notes:
Summary: Bridgepoint is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency, high-throughput inference across chat support and real-time fraud signals. They run mixed traffic: 65% short interactive chat (avg 30 tokens), 25% mid-length reranking (avg 250 tokens), 10% batch-risk scoring (avg 800 tokens).

Key latency SLO asks (from PO/infra):
- Non-streaming (request -> final token): target p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for priority routes (support agent endpoints).
- Streaming (first-byte / initial chunk): target first-byte p50 < 50ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms. Full-stream completion (last-byte) measured separately; they expect p95 < 500ms for typical 200 token replies.
- Client-side vs server-side: they want "end-to-end client roundtrip" for SLAs (includes network + client processing) but also require server-side token/timing traces for debugging and credits.

Measurement alignment notes (requested on call):
- Need a single canonical timing spec in contract: define 'latency observed' = client timestamp of final byte received - client timestamp request sent. Server will also emit server_start, server_first_byte, server_last_byte timestamps and request_id.
- Streaming measurement must include first-byte latency (for responsiveness) and last-byte latency (for completion) buckets. P99 for streaming first-byte is most critical to UX.
- Agreed to instrument request/response with trace-id and attach to Firehose logs + per-token timing in trace for root-cause.

Reserved GPU planning / throughput guarantees:
- Traffic model -> estimated steady-state reserved: 20-30 A100-equivalents for production (peak headroom to 40 GPUs).
- They want explicit tokens/sec guarantees per reserved GPU and a burst policy (x2 burst for 5 minutes) and predictable queueing behavior when capacity reached.
- Concern: batching at high concurrency can increase tail latency; they require max-queue-time config and explicit batching windows in config.

SLA negotiation points they flagged:
- SLA credit triggers tied to client-observed p99 on priority routes, with bi-directional measurement (client + server) and dispute window 14 days.
- Requested uptime SLA 99.9% for Dedicated; desire runbook and on-call contact for incidents impacting SLOs.
- Remedy: service credits *and* a technical review + remediation plan for repeat misses.

Operational asks / instrumentation:
- Per-route latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) visible in Console for both streaming and non-streaming.
- Token-level cost breakdown, per-request model variant info, and KV-cache hit rates.
- Alerting on SLO drift (7-day rolling p95/p99) + automated fallback to smaller model when latency climbs.

Quotes / customer snippets:
- "If we can show stable p99 under 300ms we can consolidate three vendor endpoints into Redwood" — Head of Payments Product
- "Need measurement that both sides trust; client-only numbers are insufficient" — Infra lead

POC ask: 2-week Dedicated slice (5 reserved GPUs) with synthetic and recorded traffic replay, Redwood to provide measurement harness + trace integration. Outcome criteria: signed measurement spec, SLO report for 100k requests, latency heatmap, and updated sizing recommendation.

Open questions:
- How does Redwood account for customer-side network variance in SLA calculation?
- Exact tokens/sec guarantee per GPU for their model family (quantized vs fp16)
- Standard SLA credit formula for p99 breaches (sliding window vs monthly aggregate)

Short-term next steps (agreed):
- Jordan to send measurement spec draft (by 2026-03-10).
- SE (Aisha) to schedule POC kickoff and request traffic replay dataset.
- Legal to pull DPA + residency commitments (SEC-77).
